header: Stereo. H C J D A 38
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE.
body: Date of hearing: 12.11.2026 Petitioner by: M/s. Ch. Mahmood-ur-Rehman, Kashif Bhatti, Mazhar Mahmood Bhatti, Ch. Abdul Razzaq and Kashif Ali Rana, Advocates for the petitioner.

Muhammad Abid, Civil Judge/Research Officer, Lahore, High Court, Lahore.

MUZAMIL AKHTAR SHABIR, J. The petitioner and respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are sister and brothers inter se. The petitioner, Mst. Musarrat Muhammad Din (‘Petitioner’), who was defendant No.2 before the trial court, through this constitution petition filed under Article 199 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1973, has called in question order dated 27.05.2025 passed by the learned Civil Judge, Chiniot, whereby in a suit for declaration filed by the respondent No.1/plaintiff, Safdar Ali (‘Respondent No.1’) through his real brother, Muhammad Yaqoob, as his next friend (‘Next Friend’) the application of respondent No.1 for temporary injunction filed under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (‘CPC’) was allowed and has also called in question order dated 17.03.2026 passed by learned Additional District Judge, Chiniot, whereby revision petition filed by the petitioner to challenge the said order has been dismissed. Both the aforesaid orders hereinafter are also referred to as (‘impugned orders’).

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner states that respondent No.1 had failed to establish prima facie case and balance of convenience in his favour and would not suffer an irreparable loss if interim relief was not granted, hence, the impugned orders having been passed against the facts of the case and law on the subject, being not sustainable are liable to be set aside.

3. Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that respondent No.1 through his real brother Muhammad Yaqub as next friend filed a suit for declaration to the effect that he is owner in possession of property (duly detailed in the headnote of the plaint) and hereinafter also referred as (‘Suit Property’) and that the relinquishment deed No.530/1, dated 25.06.2023 in favour of respondent No.2/defendant No.1 Mehboob Ali, mutation No.79885, dated 31.08.2023 and gift deed No.2357/1 dated 30.12.2023 alongwith mutation No.81030, dated 20.01.2024 regarding the suit property in favour of petitioner/defendant No.2 Musarrat Muhammad Din are result of fraud, misrepresentation and collusion. The main assertion in the contents of plaint is that respondent/plaintiff Safdar Ali is a person of unsound mind, hence unable to enter into any lawful and binding transaction; that respondent No.2 Mehboob Ali is real brother, whereas the petitioner is real sister of respondent No.1; that they started claiming their ownership right over the suit property which raised suspicion and upon perusal of relevant record by next friend of respondent No.1, the factum of impugned relinquishment deed, gift deed and mutations came on surface. Along with the suit the respondent No.1 also filed an application for interim relief restraining the respondents from further alienating the suit property during the pendency of main suit. The suit and the application for interim relief were contested by the petitioner and respondent No.2 by filing their respective written statements and replies by contending that the suit has been filed just to blackmail them and that respondent No.1 is fully conscious and capable of understanding his right and wrong and his assertion regarding unsoundness of mind is against the actual facts. Both the courts below through impugned orders have restrained the petitioner from further alienating the suit property during the pendency of the suit.

4. The question for determination before this Court is that whether the interim relief was rightly granted, especially when the claim of respondent No.1 is that he is a person of unsound mind and the petitioner has controverted the said assertion.

5. Perusal of the record shows that after hearing preliminary arguments, the learned civil court vide order dated 16.04.2024 fixed the case for 19.04.2024 for inquiry regarding unsoundness of mind/mental infirmity of respondent No.1 and maintainability of the suit through next friend. The learned civil court held an inquiry under Order XXXII Rule 15 CPC to determine authenticity of the plea of insanity and unsoundness of respondent No.1 wherein, respondent No.1 was summoned in person and examined by learned civil court. He was asked necessary questions. It was observed by the learned civil court that respondent No.1 was unable to answer any of the questions put by the court except to tell his own name and mention the fact that plaintiff and defendant are his real brothers. The learned civil court thereafter held that suit of respondent No.1 through next friend was maintainable by observing that prima facie respondent No.1 does not have capacity to understand and grasp his personal interests and vide the same order, the learned trial court passed ad-interim injunctive order directing that present petitioner shall not further alienate the suit property till the next date of hearing. On 27.05.2025 through the impugned order the learned trial court allowed the application for interim relief and confirmed the ad-interim injunctive order dated 19.04.2026 till final disposal of suit. The revision filed by the petitioner to challenge the said order has been dismissed.

6. Undisputedly, respondent No.1 was owner of the suit property, regarding which the relinquishment deed and gift deed are stated to have been allegedly executed by respondent No.1 in favour of respondent No. 2 and by respondent No.2 in favour of the petitioner, respectively, who are his brother and sister. The mental capability and legal capacity of respondent No. 1 to enter into a valid contract or lawful transaction is under question in the instant suit for declaration filed by the said respondent through next friend. It is yet to be determined whether the petitioner had the mental and legal capacity to enter into a contract or relinquish his property in favour of his brother who has transferred the property to his sister. The Supreme Court in Muhammad Zaffar Khan and another versus Syed Shumaila Zaidi and others (2025 SCMR 1961), has held as under:

‘A legally binding contract requires several elements i.e. an offer, acceptance of that offer, consideration, the parties having legal capacity to contract but not for an unlawful purpose, surely with a free consent (meeting of the minds or consensus ad idem). If the consent is procured by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake, the consent is not free.’ 7. It is yet to be determined whether the relinquishment of property was made by the free will of respondent No.1 and whether there was any consideration for the same. It is pertinent to mention here that the Supreme Court in Sadar Din versus Mst. Khatoon & others (2004 SCMR 1102) has held as under:

“4. We have gone through the record in the light of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and find that the impugned judgment of the Lahore High Court was not open to any exception. It was justifiably held by the Lahore High Court that the agreement in question through which Siraj Din had allegedly relinquished his share in the said property did not deserve any credit because the said agreement of relinquishment was without any consideration because no evidence could be led by the defendant to show that shop bearing No. E/72 was also jointly owned by Siraj Din and Sadar Din and that in consideration of Siraj Din relinquishing his share in the house in question, his brother had relinquished his share in the said shop in favour of the said Siraj Din. This document (Exh. D.1) was thus found to be nullity in the eye of law on account of section 25 of the Contract Act, 1872.
5. In this view of the matter, we find no merit in this petition which is accordingly dismissed. Leave refused.”

8. The allegation of fraud has also to be given due consideration to determine the fate of the suit for the reason that fraud vitiates most solemn of proceedings. Reliance may be placed on Pir Shah Abdul Haq (deceased) through L.Rs. and another versus Muhammad Irfan and others (2026 SCMR 1019), Faqir Ali and others versus Sakina Bibi and other (PLD 2022 SC 85).

9. It is pertinent to mention here that valuable property of respondent No. 1 is involved in the lis and, if the same is further alienated or transferred to anyone else, it will surely ensue multiplicity of litigation. Thus, the ingredient of a prima facie arguable case is fulfilled in favour of respondent No. 1. The balance of inconvenience also tilts in his favour because, if the suit property is further alienated, respondent No.1 would face much more inconvenience than the petitioner in case of grant of temporary injunction. The loss of immovable property is always considered irreparable loss and injury especially when the transfer of property is stated to be without consideration and based on fraud as agreement without consideration is void and fraud vitiates the most solemn of proceedings, hence respondent No.1 was entitled to interim relief for protection of his property.

10. For the foregoing reasons, the impugned orders passed by both the learned courts, whereby interim relief has been granted to respondent No.1, do not suffer from any kind of illegality, irregularity or jurisdictional defect rather, the same are well-reasoned and justified in the given facts of the case and have been passed to advance the cause of justice, which shall also prevent multiplicity of litigation.

11. In view of what has been discussed above, this petition being devoid of merits is dismissed. However, the observations recorded above shall not preclude the learned trial court to decide the suit on its own merits in accordance with law after recording evidence and hearing the parties. (MUZAMIL AKHTAR SHABIR)
